summary: Umatilla County, OR site: 67-ft wooden L-4 tower built 1936, torn down 1956-57; its ground cabin was moved to Tower Mountain, where it is living quarters.

facts.design: 67-foot wooden L-4 tower with a ground cabin
facts.status_note: Tower torn down by 1956 (annual report) or removed in 1957 (register); the ground cabin was moved to Tower Mountain

staffing.status: Known personnel: Mr. and Mrs. Clarence Huston (1936), Keith Hutchinson (1937); later staffing not in the sources read

visit.trail_note: About 12 miles northeast of Ukiah in the Umatilla National Forest; no source we read describes road or trail access to the site today

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umatilla National Forest

events.note: 67-foot wooden L-4 tower and ground cabin built, per the register and firelookout.com; a register panorama photo is captioned 7-25-1935 (see resolved_conflicts)

Keith Hutchinson listed as lookout personnel

By January 1951 the Lucky Strike house was set on a concrete foundation at Tower Mtn.; a garage from the site was moved to the district guard residence (Ukiah Ranger District annual report, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
January 27, 1956 annual report entry: lookout eliminated from the detection system and the tower torn down; the register and firelookout.com give 1957

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1936, but the register's panorama photo caption is dated July 25, 1935. The story uses 1936 and notes the photo date.
Forest Lookouts quotes a January 27, 1956 annual report that says the tower was torn down; the register and firelookout.com date its removal to 1957. The story reports both.

Forest Lookouts shows the house on a foundation at Tower Mtn. by January 1951. SummitPost says the Tower Mountain cabin burned in the 1940s and was replaced by this one. Both place the cabin at Tower Mountain; the exact move date is not settled.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree the tower is gone and the cabin ended up at Tower Mountain, a separate summit with its own 1935 tower. No source read describes the Lucky Strike site itself today; firelookout.com's list only covers 1936-37 staff. A geocache page for the site and a Roaming Civic Tower Mountain post were seen only as search snippets and are not cited.
